notes: Startup security self-check: the console now audits its own exposure at boot and on demand. Six read-only checks — the listening surface (is the console loopback-only, and which other services face the network), firewall exposure (a read-only backend probe that never changes a rule), access-token strength, leftover template values in the credential file, credential-file age, and file permissions qualified by what the filesystem actually enforces (network mounts report honestly instead of a fake pass). The new SECURITY card in Settings shows all six rows with an honest verdict line and a RUN CHECK button; the report is access-token gated and carries names, counts and states only — no credential value ever leaves the server. The design archive also records the follow-up static-encryption blueprint with three unlock options for a future release. Verification: console smoke grows to 499/499 and locale packs to 1380 keys per language; along the way the isolated-console end-to-end suites were hardened against live host state (a saved interface language and adopted board categories no longer leak into factory-default assertions).
